title: Reinforcement learning and hit expansion identify SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitor series
summary: A mixed workflow using deep reinforcement learning, pharmacophore and shape filters, docking and hit expansion reports three SARS-CoV-2 main-protease inhibitor series with biochemical IC50 values of 1.3–2.3 μM. The paper combines generated and commercially sourced hits; not every final inhibitor is claimed as directly model-generated. PDB entry 8R11 was released before the article and already disclosed a bound compound structure, so no priority claim is made for that structure. These biochemical findings do not establish antiviral efficacy or clinical safety.
ai_technology: Deep reinforcement learning; pharmacophore/shape filtering; docking
organization: Idorsia Pharmaceuticals; Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz

evidence.tested: Publisher abstract reports three experimentally validated Mpro inhibitor series with IC50 1.3–2.3 μM; PDB 8R11 pre-dates the paper.
evidence.unknown: Exact assignment of each final inhibitor to generated versus commercially sourced material and prior chemotype overlap not fully audited; no antiviral or clinical claims.
evidence.ai_role: Reinforcement learning generates candidate structures; computational filters and hit expansion guide follow-up, but commercially sourced hits also contributed.

source_review.scope: Primary RSC article landing page and full-text PDF abstract; first-publication date verified. PDB identity/release was reported in input ledger and should be retained as earlier structure disclosure.
